answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards unseen to the box.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; shuffle each tier and deal as specified; return unused cards unseen.

answers.answer: In four-player play the human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play the human starts at 0 VP. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; has 12 troops, with three in the garrison and nine in supply; and takes 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup 6: Score track on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; third next to board; 12 troops split 3/9; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while you still have Agents. Once you have Revealed, you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns and cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from your remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both types of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns are optional; once Revealed, your turns are skipped. Reveal effects: just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: You must pay the destination cost before resolving the space or played card effects, so resources from the Agent-box effects or destination cannot pay that entry cost. A Plot Intrigue played before Agent placement can grant resources that are available for the cost. One card sends only one Agent, using one matching Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it can be revealed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs immediately before effects; one Agent icon; no-icon cards only revealed. Player Turns: a pre-placement Plot's gains may pay entry.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited this turn may deploy, plus up to two of the four already in the garrison, for a maximum of five. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not permitted. Troops are recruited from your supply into your garrison; the current-turn recruits are eligible for deployment at a Combat space.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all units recruited during the current turn plus up to two more from garrison; cube recruits from supply into garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on a card lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at the destination, but not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy when you send an Agent to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing the Agent and before any space or card effects. You cannot use the same Spy for both effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon permits connected access without recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence is chosen immediately after placement; not the same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 2×2 for troops, 3 for the sandworm, and 4 for swords, totaling 11. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you are ineligible to play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troops 2 each, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; no Conflict unit means strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent you from playing later in the window. Combat Intrigue closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: a player need not pass just because they passed earlier; window resolves after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply, sandworms to bank, markers to 0.

answers.answer: In four-player play, two tied for first each take the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. In three-player play, the tied players each take the second reward, there are no other rewards, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in four players leaves others competing for third; with three or fewer no other rewards. No winner on tie means no card; 0 strength receives none.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles the rewards you take; a second worm does not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP or pay 6 spice for 2 VP under doubling.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; control and battle icons excluded; may pay a reward cost a second time (3 spice for 1 VP example).

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. If a battle icon matches, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three battle icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: take won card face up, then check mandatory battle-icon match. Battle Icons: face-up Conflict or Objective cards; Endgame wild match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP. Tying the current holder at 4 does not take the Alliance; a challenger must rise above the holder. Alliance VP follows the token and transfers with it.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP reverses below 2; 4 track bonus retained; Alliance goes to first at 4 and tie does not steal it—must rise above.

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it from multiple sources to buy one card and split one source across different purchases. After buying a Row card, refill the Row and you may buy its replacement if you can afford it. The acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: may use Persuasion before/between/after effects; pool or split; Row always refills; acquired card goes face up to discard.

answers.answer: On a Maker space, an Agent gains all accumulated bonus spice, in addition to the space's choice of base spice or worm option. The usual worm icon requires a Maker Hooks token when specified; Hooks are retained, not spent. Worms cannot enter a garrison. While the Shield Wall remains, no worm can be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin; after it is removed, any Conflict may receive a worm.
answers.evidence: Sandworms: Hooks are a stated requirement, not spent; Wall protects three locations. Maker spaces grant all bonus spice; wall removal permits summoning to any Conflict.

answers.answer: At Recall, if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP. Resource tiebreakers, in order, are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Recall checks 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck. Scoring: resolve Endgame Intrigue first; tiebreakers spice, Solari, water, garrison troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM shuffles all 20 standard contracts, exposes two face up, and leaves 18 face down in the bank. Add four CHOAM Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four CHOAM Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left in the box and are not part of this setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: without Shaddam, shuffle all 20 (two offers, 18 bank); add four cards to each deck; Shaddam optional; contrasting-back set excluded.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon takes an available public face-up contract and refills the offer from the bank if possible; if no public contracts remain, it gives 2 Solari instead. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining its specified total spice during that turn. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take public contract and refill, or gain 2 Solari if offers exhausted. Completing contracts lists Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire TSMS conditions.

answers.answer: No. A board-space contract must already be held when you send the Agent there, so one taken after visiting that space waits for a future turn. Upon completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: if taken after sending the Agent to that space, wait until a future turn. On completion announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival receives the Ornithopter Objective; the two humans get the other eligible Objectives at random, and the human whose card shows First Player takes the marker. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns but never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: one shared scoring Rival; Rival gets Ornithopter; humans' objectives and First Player; order stated; Rival never takes a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: If the indicated destination is occupied, the Rival ignores it and reveals again. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: use an empty post of its specified type if available, otherwise ignore the placement; in either case reveal another Hagal card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs and effects, applying only the Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy does not place Agent; normal costs/effects ignored; reshuffle immediately on empty deck or Reshuffle.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after removing those marked for the wrong player count; deal one eligible Objective face up to each player, and its First Player marker selects First Player. Shaddam may be chosen only when using the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objective cards, shuffle and deal one face up to each player. Shaddam is not used unless playing CHOAM.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water, and sandworms are not meant to be limited; if the bank runs out, make a convenient substitution. If your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource payments go back to the common bank; you do not take gains from another player's supply.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: resources and sandworms are not limited; substitute if needed; gains come from bank and payments return to bank. Recruiting: empty supply prevents recruitment.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, and Recall. At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card, resolve the defensive troop bonus if applicable, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to their Leaders; in 3–4 player games First Player passes clockwise, while in 2P Rival Agents return to supply and First Player passes to the other human.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists all five phases and Round Start steps; Recall states player count-specific Agent return and First Player handling.

answers.answer: Yes, after paying the entry cost and meeting requirements, you may resolve the space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects in any order. No, Influence from the visit cannot meet its own entry requirement because requirements and costs must be satisfied before the space effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs/meet requirements first, then effects; space, Agent-box and Influence effects may be done in any order.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost and its effect can normally be used only once per turn, so you cannot pay it twice for twice the effect; doubled Conflict rewards are the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory, except effects marked may, optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon; direct self-trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play the Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Arrows: pay and gain only once per turn, except doubled Conflict rewards. FAQ: most effects mandatory; listed exceptions; Intrigue conditions and costs must be met.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect names an Agent-icon type that must connect to the post, use only a post connected to that icon; otherwise you cannot place it.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: place at unoccupied post; if none in supply may recall one for no effect; specified icon connection can restrict placement.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player's Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy still requires playing a card for the Agent turn and does not waive costs or requirements. No, two Spies cannot both be used for Gather Intelligence on the same placement (although two may be recalled for distinct Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence effects).
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate cannot bypass your Agent; FAQ says recall still requires Agent-turn card; not two to Gather Intelligence on same placement.

answers.answer: The controller gets the location bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin; this is separate from the visitor's effects. Winning the corresponding Conflict places your Control marker and replaces the opponent's. When that controlled-location Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without visiting the space.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: bonuses whenever any player visits; winner takes control. Round Start: controller may deploy one troop from supply on reveal.

answers.answer: On a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and Conflict card, with no further rewards. Tied third-place players get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody takes the Conflict card, and no other rewards are given, including to a fourth player.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and tie table: tie for second gets third reward; tie for third nothing; three tied first gets second reward each and no other rewards/card.

answers.answer: With three different positive strengths in a three-player game, first and second receive their rewards; third receives nothing. This is the same when the Rival is one of the three participants in a standard two-player game.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 2–3 players, including human plus Rival, ordinary first and second receive rewards; untied third gets nothing; 0 strength none.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and look at them freely; reveal only when playing, then put resolved Intrigues face up in a discard pile beside the Intrigue Deck. If that deck empties, shuffle its discard to make a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards: timing by type, kept face down separately, resolved cards face up in discard. FAQ: shuffle discard if deck runs out.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifies Intrigues; it discards a card of your choice from your hand, not from play or discard pile. Secrets steals one Intrigue chosen at random from each opponent who has at least four Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand and not Intrigue unless specified. Secrets/Steal Intrigue: each opponent at 4+ gives one selected at random.

answers.answer: A trash effect may remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or instructed to trash itself; The Spice Must Flow's acquired VP remains even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing section lists sources, destinations, and optionality; FAQ says TSMS acquire VP retained after trashing.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once, when you acquire the card. Reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck whenever you cannot draw because your deck is empty. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box: at acquisition, not play. Acquiring Cards: reshuffle when unable to draw; Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn stay face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond cards may activate if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They stop being in play when moved to discard at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: definition, mutual activation regardless of order, and Clean Up timing.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed this turn; it may be used again on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop returns from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits retreating zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon: other Agent, reusable this round. Retreat: troop to garrison; FAQ says retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect that grants two Influence must put both with one chosen Faction; it cannot split them. An Alliance-icon effect requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token, and a minimum-Influence effect requires the stated threshold with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence rules: gain two free-choice cannot choose two Factions; Alliance icon requires token; some effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which of the formerly tied opponents receives the Alliance. If the holder drops to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the Alliance to the board; the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Influence and FAQ: if several were tied, former holder chooses recipient; at 3 or lower with nobody at 4+, return token and lose VP.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the normal five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until that point, is used, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing: during Reveal means immediately reveal/use; after Reveal keep for next round; later Reveal Plot remains face up then discards.

answers.answer: No. Tying for first is not winning, so you cannot play a “when you win” Intrigue after the tie. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops: cannot play “when you win” after tying first; if received as winning reward may play immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12, the printed track's end.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Victory: all four tiebreakers tied goes to most recent Reveal; scores may exceed printed 12.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with the one Agent placement. Their effects are another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects; you must have held each contract when sending the Agent there.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion: fulfill all same-space contracts with one placement; resolve in any order; must hold at placement.

answers.answer: No. Shaddam sets aside both Sardaukar contracts during setup; they are reserved for his exclusive acquisition but do not begin in his possession. When he acquires a contract, he may choose one of the reserved contracts instead of a public one. His Signet Ring deployment restriction applies immediately and lasts for that turn only.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup and Reserved Sardaukar contracts; Shaddam clarification: restriction immediately on Signet Ring Agent turn and lasts only turn.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of the Training track and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd token initial/final position; Lady Jessica starts face up; Reverend Mother may act on flip turn.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 Influence counts as reaching 2. You can trigger it again with the same Faction after losing Influence and later moving up through 2 again; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: passing 2 while gaining counts; can reach again when moving up, not down. Guild's Favor Clean Up is not discard-triggering.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, has no cost, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM gain 2 Solari; with CHOAM take an available public contract, or gain 2 Solari if offers are exhausted. It is not a Faction space and gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost, gains 1 Emperor Influence plus the same contract-icon effect; its automatic Emperor advance is that one Influence counted once.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: shared contract icon rule and table for Accept Contract/Dutiful Service; contract spaces clarify faction status.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no entry cost, Combat yes; controller gains 1 Solari, visitor recruits one troop and draws one card. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station rows.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and Hagga Basin costs 1 water. Deep Desert offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. At either space you gain all accumulated bonus spice as well. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide lists costs/base choices; Maker rules grant all bonus spice; FAQ says Hooks retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and at least 2 Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. Option two gains 1 water and optionally removes the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr requirements and two choices.

answers.answer: Each visit costs 5 Solari and the space is not a Combat space. On the first visit, put your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On later visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 Solari after anyone does. Each player may take it only once per game. Take the third Agent onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row, including Rival clarification.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses the Landsraad icon, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence because it is not an Emperor Faction space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege row; Landsraad is not a Faction.

answers.answer: Shipping uses the Spice Trade icon, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access and is not a Combat space: choose 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if you pay 2, also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access and is a Combat space: choose 0 or 1 spice to gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner uses Spacing Guild access, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is a Combat space and permits normal deployment. Desert Tactics uses Fremen access, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and optionally trashes a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar uses Emperor access, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar and Combat column.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad access, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild access, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: Affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. False Orders may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Ignore Litany Against Fear's red box during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ—False Orders and Litany Against Fear clarifications.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Manipulate: opponents cannot acquire; you may by other means without discount; remove after next Reveal if unacquired.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottoms of the Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and the remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining the 2P Reshuffle card and put the deck near the Rival. The Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup: Rival components, water, 0 score/Combat; retain Reshuffle; 10+ VP triggers Endgame just like human.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that amount and takes its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water in supply, including starting water, each unit/card as one. Spend in mandatory order: Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, then water, using as much as needed and keeping leftovers. Its Agent is available immediately in the current round.
answers.evidence: Rival Swordmaster resource total and mandatory spending priority; take third Agent usable in current round.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot combine a mixed total of seven resources; only those exact sets count.
answers.evidence: After Swordmaster: specified separate resource sets for 1 VP.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival picks the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by leftmost priority. It gets the 2-Influence VP and Alliance VP like a human, but does not receive the resource track bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in the Rival card's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: least Influence, leftmost tie; Alliances and Influence VP like human, no 4-Influence resource bonus; numbered icon definition.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination card, select only the destination matching current conditions; if occupied, reveal another card and do not use the other destination. Accept Contract/Shipping selection depends on Guild Influence, while Deliver Supplies/Heighliner depends on Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: condition selection for two-destination cards and occupied destination handling.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if that Hagal card recruited none, as well as newly recruited troops. At a noncombat space, recruited troops go into the garrison. An unmet conditional 2+ Influence bonus does not prevent Agent placement; simply omit that bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and Combat-space deployment; 2+ bonus does not prevent placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, place a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy immediately recalls the Rival's other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: priority order, all occupied, third Spy effect, no Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival places its Agent at a Combat space that same turn, those troops are also deployed there. If a Place Spy card has no legal post, ignore placement, then reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies/Schemes: Scheme recruits before placement also deploy; Place Spy no legal post still reveals another card.

answers.answer: The Rival always takes all accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga with Hooks and an unprotected Conflict it summons one worm instead of the 2 base spice; at Deep Desert it summons two instead of 4. Without Hooks, or when the Conflict is protected by the Shield Wall, it summons none and takes the base spice instead. Hooks are the Rival's own token.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: all bonus spice; Hooks and wall condition; if no worms, take Hagga 2 or Deep Desert 4.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window and can respond. A Rival with no deployed unit does not get the bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: strength bonus timing, bottom swords only, reshuffle response, unit requirement; humans then Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes: the Rival can gain control bonuses, deploy a defensive troop from supply when its controlled Conflict is revealed, win Conflict cards and battle-icon VP, and double rewards with worms. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: control, defensive troop, doubled rewards, battle icons, optional VP, and contract handling.

answers.answer: During Reveal-effect resolution, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed during that Reveal turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn timing lets strength be set at any point while resolving; Strength section describes over-20 marker.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Cards of any type can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader rules: Signet Ring-marked right ability activates when Signet Ring is played on Agent turn; overview says cards can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply. It does not itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recall effects chosen without a card, while a Recall Spy card icon is resolved as specified by that card.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon returns a Spy to supply, usually as cost for a powerful effect; separate recall effects described.

answers.answer: The distinct trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from hand but cannot choose an Intrigue unless specified; discarding does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding: hand card and Intrigue exclusion.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm doubling lets you pay the reward cost a second time; a doubled reward of 1 Influence can therefore be gained twice, with the same or two different Factions. By contrast, a single effect granting two free-choice Influence requires both with one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm reward example allows 2 Influence with same or two different Factions; Influence rules say a gain-two free-choice icon cannot split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card's printed Signet Ring ability. The Hagal Signet Ring icon triggers that ability directly; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is involved. The Scheme is triggered separately when it places its third/final supply Spy.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme table distinguishes triggers; Hagal Signet resolves Signet ability.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival a token only if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no extra token. Shield Wall removal works only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks, ignore it; if the Wall is already gone, it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table lists each condition.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gains 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws one Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; each opponent with at least four Intrigues gives one Intrigue chosen at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row; Steal Intrigue rule specifies opponents at four or more and random selection.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there; if that same visitor controls it, the controller bonus is an additional 1 spice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin row; controlled-location bonuses apply whenever any player, including self, visits.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any still-unclaimed Conflict cards from previous rounds. Then resolve the controlled-location defensive troop bonus, if any, and each player draws five cards; thus Conflict reveal precedes the round's hand draw.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal and place atop any remaining cards; resolve defensive bonus; then each player draws five.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks; the Alliance tokens start on their marked spaces on those four tracks, so no human begins holding an Alliance. The Shield Wall token is placed on its marked area below Spice Refinery at setup.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on tracks, Shield Wall on board, each player's four cubes at bottom spaces.

answers.answer: First Player takes the first turn, then play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. Players may continue Agent turns until choosing one Reveal; after Revealing, they are skipped. In 3–4 player play, Player Turns ends when all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, First Player goes first and priority continues clockwise; each eligible player may play any number before passing, and prior passes do not prevent a later play. The window ends after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections: clockwise order, end condition, First Player priority, any number cards and consecutive-pass closure.

answers.answer: The three steps are Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve the revealed cards' Reveal boxes and Persuasion purchases; set strength), then Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). You choose the order of Reveal-box effects; they need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists three steps; Resolve effects may be done in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's ten-card starting deck face down: Convincing Argument×2, Dagger×2, Dune, the Desert Planet×2, Diplomacy, Reconnaissance, Seek Allies, Signet Ring; place it face down to the Leader's left. Without CHOAM omit marked cards, shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, deal five face-up Imperium cards to the Row, and put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, and Control markers start in the player's supply.
answers.evidence: Components/Starting deck and Setup steps 4, 6: deck lists and states, deck preparation, Row/Reserve, marker and components in supply.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, spend Persuasion on any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. The cost is at the card's top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases happen during Reveal, before, between, or after Reveal effects.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: eligible Row and Reserve cards, top-right cost, purchases during Reveal and timing around effects.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, so you may decline even with a legal placement or recall. Shield Wall destruction is also optional (“may remove”); once returned to the box it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Spies: placement and Recall icons optional. Shield Wall: may remove; gone for rest of game and cannot return.

answers.answer: Normally the played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a card with only City access send an Agent there. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, it can access any space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spy Agent rules: matching normal icon required, or Spy Agent icon plus connected Spy; a connected Spy alone does not grant access.

answers.answer: Yes. You may first play a legal Plot Intrigue during your Agent turn before placing the Agent; resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources from the card played to send the Agent or from the destination occur after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: pre-placement Plot gains may pay; gains after placement from destination or played Agent card cannot pay that entry.

answers.answer: No. Even after both humans have Revealed, Player Turns continues with the Rival's remaining Agent turns while it still has Agents in supply. The Rival never Reveals; Combat begins only once both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents.
answers.evidence: Two-player Player Turns: continue Rival Agent turns after human Reveals; proceed to Combat after both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit; taking the bonus is optional. After Combat rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before the Makers phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start controlled-space bonus; Critical Locations; Combat cleanup resets all Combat markers to 0.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve that card's Agent box, ignoring its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile for this turn, nor move an Agent already on the board as the Agent sent; the turn uses a card from hand and an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play a card from hand; send Agent from Leader; card face up; use Agent box. Recall Agent is separately an effect for another Agent.

answers.answer: The restriction already applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot postpone it by resolving the space effects first. It prevents deploying units to the Conflict for that entire turn.
answers.evidence: Shaddam clarification: Emperor restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring to send Agent; ordering effects cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: With four distinct positive strengths, first, second, and third receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up into their supply, then checks battle-icon matches.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in four-player games first, second, third can receive rewards; fourth none; winner takes card.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from the discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw from own deck; if empty shuffle discard; no chosen discard option.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place its deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck. Do not remove it.
answers.evidence: Rival setup: shuffle House Hagal and place near Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When acquired, move a token from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: all Maker Hooks in common bank; later acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: The Combat marker must be adjusted when the Combat Intrigue resolves during the Combat Intrigue window; the Reveal-turn value is not fixed. Use the adjusted strength on the track to resolve Combat rewards.
answers.evidence: Combat: Combat Intrigue changes to units/strength require marker adjustment when that card resolves; adjusted track strength is used.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the common bank. You may not take them from another player's supply; if the bank runs out, use a convenient substitution because resources are not meant to be limited.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: resource gains from bank; bank is not limited, substitute if needed.

answers.answer: Shuffle the contract tokens face down before revealing two face-up offers; the rest remain face down in the bank. Players do not choose which offers appear or preset the hidden order—the tokens are shuffled.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle the 20 standard contracts face down, then flip two face up and put remainder face down in bank.

answers.answer: Before the contract shuffle, set aside both Sardaukar contracts for Shaddam's exclusive acquisition; they do not start in his possession. Shuffle the remaining 18, expose two face up, and put 16 face down in the bank. Only Shaddam may later choose one of the reserved contracts when acquiring a contract.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup with Shaddam: set aside both Sardaukar contracts, shuffle remaining 18 into two offers and 16 bank; Reserved Sardaukar contracts section.
